model.name: ISO 22301 Business Continuity (starter)
model.documentation: A business continuity management system (BCMS) traced from the requirements of ISO 22301:2019 (clauses 4 to 10) to the work that meets them, and from there to an example organisation's prioritised activities. Each activity carries its recovery time objective, maximum tolerable period of disruption, recovery point objective and minimum business continuity objective, set by the business impact analysis, and is linked to the applications, technology, people and suppliers it depends on and to the continuity strategy and plan that protect it. Because every dependency is connected, the model answers what stops, and how soon it must be back, when a system or supplier fails. Clause numbers and titles are given for reference only; read the requirements in the standard itself. Replace the example online retailer with your own activities and recovery objectives.

element.name: ISO 22301:2019 Business continuity management systems
element.documentation: The international standard for a business continuity management system, read with Amendment 1:2024 on climate action changes. Certification is against clauses 4 to 10.

element.name: Top management
element.documentation: Owns the business continuity policy and objectives, and reviews the management system at planned intervals.

element.name: Keep prioritised activities within their recovery objectives
element.documentation: Continue delivering products and services at an acceptable, agreed capacity during a disruption, and recover them within the agreed time.

element.name: ISO 22301 requirements (clauses 4 to 10)
element.documentation: The requirements a certified management system must meet.

element.name: Clause 4: Context of the organisation
element.documentation: Know the organisation, its interested parties and their legal and regulatory requirements, and set the scope of the management system.

element.name: Clause 5: Leadership
element.documentation: Top management commits to the management system, sets a business continuity policy and assigns roles, responsibilities and authorities.

element.name: Clause 6: Planning
element.documentation: Address risks and opportunities, set business continuity objectives with plans to achieve them, and plan changes to the management system.

element.name: Clause 7: Support
element.documentation: Provide resources, competence, awareness, communication and documented information.

element.name: Clause 9: Performance evaluation
element.documentation: Monitor, measure, analyse and evaluate, run internal audits and hold management reviews.

element.name: Clause 10: Improvement
element.documentation: Handle nonconformities with corrective action and improve the management system continually.

element.name: Clause 8: Operation
element.documentation: Plan and run the business continuity processes: impact analysis, risk assessment, strategies, plans, exercises and evaluation.

element.name: 8.1 Operational planning and control
element.documentation: Plan, run and control the processes the management system needs, including outsourced processes and the supply chain.

element.name: 8.2 Business impact analysis and risk assessment
element.documentation: Analyse the impact of disrupting each activity over time, set recovery priorities and objectives, and assess the risks of disruption.

element.name: 8.3 Business continuity strategies and solutions
element.documentation: Identify, select and put in place the strategies and resources that meet the recovery objectives.

element.name: 8.4 Business continuity plans and procedures
element.documentation: Set up a response structure, warning and communication arrangements, and documented plans for response and recovery.

element.name: 8.5 Exercise programme
element.documentation: Exercise and test the strategies and plans on a schedule, and act on what the exercises show.

element.name: 8.6 Evaluation of business continuity documentation and capabilities
element.documentation: Evaluate whether the impact analysis, risk assessment, strategies, plans and suppliers' capabilities remain suitable and effective.

view.name: BCMS requirements by clause
view.documentation: Clauses 4 to 10 of ISO 22301, with clause 8 opened into its six operational subclauses, each with the control that realizes it. Fill in the owner and evidence location of every control; that pair is what a certification auditor asks for first.

view.name: Prioritised activities and their dependencies
view.documentation: Read top to bottom: each prioritised activity with its recovery objectives, the applications and services it needs, what they run on, and the contract and supplier behind each. Any activity whose chain ends in a supplier with no tested exit plan, or in a single site, cannot recover faster than that supplier or site.

view.name: Continuity strategies and plans
view.documentation: The business impact analysis sets the recovery objectives of each prioritised activity; each activity is protected by one or more continuity strategies, and each strategy is carried out from a documented plan. An activity with no strategy, or a plan never exercised, is the gap to close first.

view.name: What breaks if the cloud provider fails
view.documentation: The chain an impact question walks: supplier, contract, hosting service, the two applications on it, the prioritised activities they serve with their recovery objectives, and the strategy that is meant to bring them back.
